episodes.188278: Several rounds of severe thunderstorms produced numerous reports of large hail and wind damage.
episodes.189197: Heavy rain in mid-March brought a period of river flooding to central and southern Arkansas where minor flood stage was recorded on the Fourche LaFave, Saline, and Ouachita River basins.
episodes.189324: A weak shortwave trough provided sufficient lift to generate isolated thunderstorms. One of these storms produced large hail.
episodes.190017: Several thunderstorms developed along the Rio Grande southwest of San Antonio late in the day on March 16th. Those storms tracked northeast across the Texas coastline towards Louisiana, riding along a stalled frontal boundary. Although this front provided a focus to maintain storms, surface heated in southwest Louisiana started the main enhancement of convection on the 17th. The storms eventually organized into a Mesoscale Convective System which resulted in a severe thunderstorm in the open Gulf waters south of Louisiana.
episodes.190118: A cold front slowly approaches South Texas from the north, leaving the region in the favorable warm sector with mid-level disturbances aiding in convection. A supercell capable of producing large hail over McMullen and Live Oak Counties occurred during the morning of the 15th. A couple large supercells over eastern Mexico diminished but maintained severe intensity as they moved eastward into Webb County late in the evening of the 15th. Another round of severe storms moved eastward from the Brush Country to the Coastal Plains the night of the 16th into the midday hours of the 17th. A unwarned severe wind gust of 60 mph was reported on the evening of the 15th at KCOT and a golf ball size hail was reported in McMullen County on the morning of the 17th.
